title: 02. Networking, Protocols & APIs: REST API
summary: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style for distributed hypermedia systems built on six constraints — client-server, stateless, cacheable, uniform interface, layered, and code-on-demand (optional) —…
objectives: What are the six constraints of REST, and why does each one matter?
What is idempotency in REST, and how do you make POST safe to retry?
How do you version a REST API, and what are the trade-offs of each approach?
What is HATEOAS, and why is it rarely used in practice?

sections.title: Explanation
sections.body:
> **In one line:** REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style for distributed hypermedia systems built on six constraints — client-server, stateless, cacheable, uniform interface, layered, and code-on-demand (optional) — that together produce APIs that are simple, scalable, and evolvable over years.
REST was distilled by Roy Fielding in his 2000 PhD dissertation from the design choices that made the web (HTTP, URIs, media types) scale to billions of pages. The core idea: model your domain as a set of **resources** (nouns like `/users/42`, `/orders/1007`, `/products/sku-77`), expose them through a **uniform interface** (HTTP verbs GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE acting on those nouns), let the server return **representations** (JSON, XML, HTML — the same resource can have many representations), and use hypermedia links (HATEOAS) to drive the client through state transitions without hardcoding URLs. The six constraints each solve a specific problem. **Client-server** separates UI concerns from data storage, letting them evolve independently. **Stateless** means every request contains all context the server needs (no server-side sessions); this is what enables horizontal scaling — any backend instance can serve any request because there is no per-instance state. **Cacheable** means responses explicitly declare whether they can be cached (`Cache-Control: max-age=300`), letting CDNs and reverse proxies serve subsequent requests without touching the origin. **Uniform interface** is the contract: HTTP methods have fixed semantics (GET is safe, PUT/DELETE are idempotent, POST is neither), status codes have fixed meaning (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 404 Not Found, 409 Conflict, 422 Unprocessable Entity, 500 Internal Server Error). **Layered** means a client cannot tell whether it is talking to the origin or to a proxy/CDN/gateway in front of it; this lets you insert caches, load balancers, and security layers without changing the client. **Code-on-demand** (optional) means the server can ship executable code (JavaScript) to the client — the only optional constraint, used by browsers but rarely by API clients.

REST matters because it is the lingua franca of the public internet. The GitHub REST API v3, Stripe API, Twitter API v1.1/v2, Slack Web API, AWS REST APIs, and the vast majority of internal microservices all use REST over HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 with JSON. REST's virtues: it uses the same protocol the web already runs on (no new infrastructure), it is human-readable (you can `curl` it from a terminal), it is cacheable by standard HTTP infrastructure (CDNs, browser caches, reverse proxies), and it is stateless so backends scale horizontally without session affinity. REST's costs: it is verbose compared to binary protocols like gRPC (JSON is text, with field names repeated in every payload), it does not have built-in streaming (HTTP/1.1 is request-response), and the lack of a schema means clients and servers must coordinate informally on payload shape — which is why OpenAPI/Swagger specs, JSON Schema, and tools like Pact emerged.

Real-world deployments illustrate the patterns. **Stripe**'s REST API is a textbook example: every mutable resource has a stable URL (`/v1/charges/ch_xxx`), every write operation accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header so retries are safe (the same key returns the same response without double-charging), and every error returns a structured JSON body with `error.type`, `error.code`, `error.param`, and `error.decline_code` so clients can programmatically branch. **GitHub**'s REST API v3 enforces rate limits via `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers and uses ETags for conditional requests (`If-None-Match` returns 304 Not Modified when nothing changed — saving bandwidth and backend work). **Twitter** v2 uses pagination cursors (`meta.next_token`) instead of offset, because offset pagination becomes O(n) at high offsets. **Netflix**'s internal microservices use REST for the bulk of synchronous calls (with gRPC for high-throughput paths), versioned via URL prefix (`/v3/`) so breaking changes ship without breaking existing clients. **Amazon** S3 is REST: PUT object, GET object, DELETE object, LIST bucket — the entire storage system is exposed as HTTP verbs on URL resources.

The trade-offs and pitfalls deserve attention. First, **versioning** — once an API is public, you cannot change it without breaking clients. Strategies: URL versioning (`/v1/`, `/v2/` — simplest, but creates a new namespace), header versioning (`Accept: application/vnd.example.v2+json` — keeps URLs clean, but harder to test in a browser), and query-param versioning (`?version=2` — avoid, breaks caching). Stripe and GitHub use URL versioning because it is explicit and cacheable. Second, **idempotency** — GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent by HTTP spec; POST and PATCH are not. For POST operations that must be safe to retry (payment creation, order submission), use an `Idempotency-Key` header so the server dedupes retries (Stripe's pattern). Third, **HATEOAS** — Fielding's strict REST requires that clients follow hypermedia links returned by the server, never hardcoding URLs. In practice, HATEOAS is rarely implemented because it is verbose and the payoff is small for internal APIs; it is more common in public APIs where client diversity is high (e.g., Spring Data REST auto-generates HATEOAS responses). Fourth, **Richardson Maturity Model** — Level 0 (HTTP as a tunnel, e.g., SOAP over HTTP), Level 1 (resources, but everything is POST), Level 2 (HTTP verbs and status codes used correctly), Level 3 (HATEOAS). Most production APIs sit at Level 2. Fifth, **N+1 problem** — a client listing 100 orders then fetching each order's user makes 101 round-trips; mitigate with compound resources (`/orders?expand=user`), GraphQL (Phase 2 Topic 11), or pre-joined views. REST connects to many other system design concepts: it sits on top of HTTP (Phase 2 Topic 3) and HTTPS (Phase 2 Topic 4), is fronted by reverse proxies and API gateways (Phase 2 Topic 8 and Phase 8), is cached by CDNs (Phase 2 Topic 7), competes with and complements GraphQL (Phase 2 Topic 11) and gRPC (Phase 2 Topic 12), and its idempotency-key pattern is foundational to distributed retries (Phase 7 reliability).

### Mermaid Diagram ```mermaid flowchart LR C[Client] -->|GET /v1/users/42| API C -->|POST /v1/orders + Idempotency-Key| API API[REST API server
stateless] DB[(database)] API --> DB API -->|ETag / Last-Modified| C API -->|"201 Created + Location: /v1/orders/1007"| C API -->|422 + error json| C API -->|"Cache-Control: max-age=300"| CDN[CDN cache] CDN -.->|cached GET response| C style API fill:#c4f9d0 style CDN fill:#fef3c7 ``` ### ASCII Diagram ``` +----------+ | Client | curl -X POST https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges \ +-----+----+ -H "Idempotency-Key: abc123" -d amount=1000 | | HTTPS request (stateless: all context in the request) v +------------------------------------------+ | REST API server (stateless) | | +-------+ +-------+ +------+ +------+ | | | route | | auth | | valid| | idem | | | | | | (JWT) | | ate | | dedup| | | +-------+ +-------+ +------+ +------+ | | +-----------------------------------+ | | | controller -> service -> repo | | | +-----------------------------------+ | +-----+------------+------------+----------+ | | | v v v +----------+ +----------+ +----------+ | database | | cache | | queue | | (users, | | (Redis) | | (Kafka) | | orders) | | | | | +----------+ +----------+ +----------+ Response codes: 200 OK GET succeeded 201 Created POST created a new resource (Location: /new/url) 204 No Content DELETE/PUT succeeded (no body) 304 Not Modified ETag match (cached response still fresh) 400 Bad Request malformed JSON / missing field 401 Unauthorized missing/invalid auth token 404 Not Found resource does not exist 409 Conflict duplicate resource 422 Unprocessable well-formed but semantically invalid 429 Too Many rate limit exceeded 500 Internal server bug 503 Unavailable backend down ``` ### Walkthrough 1. A client sends `GET /v1/users/42` to the REST API. The API server is stateless — it does not remember anything about the client between requests. The auth middleware extracts the `Authorization: Bearer ` header, validates the JWT signature and expiry, and populates the request context with the caller's identity. The router dispatches to `UserController.get_user(user_id=42)`. 2. The controller calls the service layer, which calls the repository, which queries the database for user 42. The service computes an ETag (e.g., `W/"abc123"` — a weak hash of the response body) and attaches it to the response. If the client had sent `If-None-Match: W/"abc123"` and the ETag matches, the server returns `304 Not Modified` with no body — saving bandwidth and serialization time. The response includes `Cache-Control: max-age=300` so the CDN in front of the API can serve subsequent requests for the same URL for 5 minutes without touching the origin. 3. For a `POST /v1/orders` request, the client includes an `Idempotency-Key: abc-123` header. The server stores the key in Redis with a 24-hour TTL; if the client retries the same request (because of a network timeout), the server detects the duplicate key, returns the original response (including the original order ID), and does not create a second order. This is the Stripe pattern and it is what makes REST safe to use for payments despite the unreliable network.

sections.title: Code
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Minimal Flask-style REST API with CRUD, idempotency-key dedup,
- ETag-based conditional GET, and rate limiting. Pure stdlib.
- Idempotency-key -> (status, body, expires_at)
- Seed with one user.
- Rate limiter: 10 requests / 10 seconds per client IP.
- Conditional GET: if client's If-None-Match matches, return 304.
- Idempotency-Key dedup (Stripe pattern).
- Replay the original response.

**Defines:** `User`, `Store`, `rate_limit_ok()`, `etag_of()`, `RESTHandler`, `ThreadingHTTPServer`, `run_demo()`

```python
# Minimal Flask-style REST API with CRUD, idempotency-key dedup,
# ETag-based conditional GET, and rate limiting. Pure stdlib.

import http.server
import json
import hashlib
import time
import threading
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Optional

@dataclass
class User:
    id: int
    name: str
    email: str
    updated_at: float

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {"id": self.id, "name": self.name, "email": self.email,
                "updated_at": self.updated_at}

@dataclass
class Store:
    users: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    next_id: int = 1
    # idempotency-key -> (status, body, expires_at)
    idempotency: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    lock: threading.Lock = field(default_factory=threading.Lock)

    def create_user(self, name: str, email: str) -> User:
        with self.lock:
            u = User(id=self.next_id, name=name, email=email,
                     updated_at=time.time())
            self.users[u.id] = u
            self.next_id += 1
            return u

    def get_user(self, uid: int) -> Optional[User]:
        return self.users.get(uid)

    def list_users(self) -> list:
        return list(self.users.values())

    def update_user(self, uid: int, name: str = None, email: str = None):
        u = self.users.get(uid)
        if u is None:
            return None
        if name:
            u.name = name
        if email:
            u.email = email
        u.updated_at = time.time()
        return u

    def delete_user(self, uid: int) -> bool:
        return self.users.pop(uid, None) is not None

STORE = Store()
# Seed with one user.
STORE.create_user("Ada Lovelace", "ada@example.com")

# Rate limiter: 10 requests / 10 seconds per client IP.
RATE_BUCKETS = defaultdict(lambda: {"tokens": 10.0, "last": time.time()})
RATE_CAPACITY = 10.0
RATE_REFILL = 1.0  # tokens per second

def rate_limit_ok(client_ip: str) -> bool:
    b = RATE_BUCKETS[client_ip]
    now = time.time()
    b["tokens"] = min(RATE_CAPACITY,
                      b["tokens"] + (now - b["last"]) * RATE_REFILL)
    b["last"] = now
    if b["tokens"] < 1.0:
        return False
    b["tokens"] -= 1.0
    return True

def etag_of(body: bytes) -> str:
    return 'W/"' + hashlib.md5(body).hexdigest()[:12] + '"'

class RESTHandler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        print(f"[api] {self.command} {self.path} - {fmt % args}")

    def _send(self, status: int, body: dict, extra_headers: dict = None):
        data = json.dumps(body).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data)))
        etag = etag_of(data)
        self.send_header("ETag", etag)
        if extra_headers:
            for k, v in extra_headers.items():
                self.send_header(k, v)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def _read_body(self) -> dict:
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
        if length == 0:
            return {}
        try:
            return json.loads(self.rfile.read(length).decode())
        except Exception:
            return None  # signals parse error

    def _check_rate(self) -> bool:
        client_ip = self.client_address[0]
        if not rate_limit_ok(client_ip):
            self._send(429, {"error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
                             "type": "rate_limit_error"})
            return False
        return True

    def do_GET(self):
        if not self._check_rate():
            return
        if self.path == "/v1/users":
            users = [u.to_dict() for u in STORE.list_users()]
            body = {"data": users, "count": len(users)}
            # Conditional GET: if client's If-None-Match matches, return 304.
            data = json.dumps(body).encode()
            current_etag = etag_of(data)
            if self.headers.get("If-None-Match") == current_etag:
                self.send_response(304)
                self.send_header("ETag", current_etag)
                self.end_headers()
                return
            self._send(200, body,
                       {"Cache-Control": "max-age=60"})
            return
        if self.path.startswith("/v1/users/"):
            try:
                uid = int(self.path.split("/")[-1])
            except ValueError:
                self._send(400, {"error": "invalid user id"})
                return
            u = STORE.get_user(uid)
            if u is None:
                self._send(404, {"error": "not_found",
                                 "type": "invalid_request_error"})
                return
            self._send(200, {"data": u.to_dict()})
            return
        self._send(404, {"error": "route not found"})

    def do_POST(self):
        if not self._check_rate():
            return
        if self.path != "/v1/users":
            self._send(404, {"error": "route not found"})
            return
        body = self._read_body()
        if body is None:
            self._send(400, {"error": "invalid JSON",
                             "type": "invalid_request_error"})
            return
        # Validate required fields.
        missing = [f for f in ("name", "email") if f not in body]
        if missing:
            self._send(422, {"error": "validation_failed",
                             "type": "invalid_request_error",
                             "missing": missing})
            return
        # Idempotency-Key dedup (Stripe pattern).
        idem_key = self.headers.get("Idempotency-Key")
        if idem_key:
            cached = STORE.idempotency.get(idem_key)
            if cached and cached[2] > time.time():
                # Replay the original response.
                self._send(cached[0], cached[1],
                           {"Location": f"/v1/users/{cached[1]['data']['id']}",
                            "Idempotency-Replay": "true"})
                return
        u = STORE.create_user(body["name"], body["email"])
        resp_body = {"data": u.to_dict()}
        if idem_key:
            STORE.idempotency[idem_key] = (
                201, resp_body, time.time() + 24 * 3600)
        self._send(201, resp_body,
                   {"Location": f"/v1/users/{u.id}"})

    def do_PATCH(self):
        if not self._check_rate():
            return
        if not self.path.startswith("/v1/users/"):
            self._send(404, {"error": "route not found"})
            return
        try:
            uid = int(self.path.split("/")[-1])
        except ValueError:
            self._send(400, {"error": "invalid user id"})
            return
        body = self._read_body()
        if body is None:
            self._send(400, {"error": "invalid JSON"})
            return
        u = STORE.update_user(uid, body.get("name"), body.get("email"))
        if u is None:
            self._send(404, {"error": "not_found"})
            return
        self._send(200, {"data": u.to_dict()})

    def do_DELETE(self):
        if not self._check_rate():
            return
        if not self.path.startswith("/v1/users/"):
            self._send(404, {"error": "route not found"})
            return
        try:
            uid = int(self.path.split("/")[-1])
        except ValueError:
            self._send(400, {"error": "invalid user id"})
            return
        if STORE.delete_user(uid):
            self.send_response(204)
            self.end_headers()
        else:
            self._send(404, {"error": "not_found"})

class ThreadingHTTPServer(http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer):
    daemon_threads = True

def run_demo():
    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8080), RESTHandler)
    threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
    print("[demo] REST API listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080")

    import urllib.request, urllib.error
    base = "http://127.0.0.1:8080"

    def req(method, path, body=None, headers=None):
        data = json.dumps(body).encode() if body else None
        r = urllib.request.Request(f"{base}{path}", data=data, method=method)
        if data:
            r.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        for k, v in (headers or {}).items():
            r.add_header(k, v)
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(r, timeout=2) as resp:
                return resp.status, dict(resp.headers), \
                       json.loads(resp.read().decode() or "{}")
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            return e.code, dict(e.headers), \
                   json.loads(e.read().decode() or "{}")

    print("\n--- 1. GET /v1/users (list) ---")
    s, h, b = req("GET", "/v1/users")
    etag1 = h.get("ETag")
    print(f"  status={s} count={b.get('count')} etag={etag1}")

    print("\n--- 2. GET /v1/users with If-None-Match (expect 304) ---")
    s, h, b = req("GET", "/v1/users", headers={"If-None-Match": etag1})
    print(f"  status={s} (expect 304 Not Modified)")

    print("\n--- 3. POST /v1/users (create) ---")
    s, h, b = req("POST", "/v1/users",
                  body={"name": "Grace Hopper", "email": "grace@example.com"},
                  headers={"Idempotency-Key": "key-001"})
    print(f"  status={s} (expect 201) location={h.get('Location')} "
          f"new_id={b['data']['id']}")

    print("\n--- 4. POST again with same Idempotency-Key (expect replay) ---")
    s, h, b = req("POST", "/v1/users",
                  body={"name": "Grace Hopper", "email": "grace@example.com"},
                  headers={"Idempotency-Key": "key-001"})
    print(f"  status={s} (expect 201) replay={h.get('Idempotency-Replay')} "
          f"same_id={b['data']['id']}")

    print("\n--- 5. POST with missing fields (expect 422) ---")
    s, h, b = req("POST", "/v1/users", body={"name": "No Email"})
    print(f"  status={s} (expect 422) error={b.get('error')} "
          f"missing={b.get('missing')}")

    print("\n--- 6. GET /v1/users/999 (expect 404) ---")
    s, h, b = req("GET", "/v1/users/999")
    print(f"  status={s} (expect 404) error={b.get('error')}")

    print("\n--- 7. PATCH /v1/users/2 (update) ---")
    s, h, b = req("PATCH", "/v1/users/2", body={"email": "grace@navy.mil"})
    print(f"  status={s} (expect 200) new_email={b['data']['email']}")

    print("\n--- 8. DELETE /v1/users/2 (expect 204) ---")
    s, h, b = req("DELETE", "/v1/users/2")
    print(f"  status={s} (expect 204 No Content)")

    server.shutdown()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_demo()
```
